rows.subtype: Approach: stabilise first, diagnose later [Thinking]
rows.description: During a payments outage, the on-call engineer chooses to roll back the latest release at once instead of hunting the bug, because customers are failing to pay every minute.

rows.subtype: Approach: working through a runbook [Action]
rows.description: The engineer follows a written checklist: check dashboards, recent deployments, database health and dependencies, in order, which speeds diagnosis when the mind is stressed at three in the morning.

rows.subtype: Approach: everyone trying random fixes at once [Pitfall]
rows.description: Five engineers change settings simultaneously without telling one another. The system state becomes unclear, and it is impossible to know which change helped or hurt.

rows.subtype: Approach: blameless postmortem [Revision]
rows.description: After recovery, the team writes a timeline, finds root causes in the missing alert and untested rollback, and lists actions with owners, focusing on system improvements not on punishing individuals.

rows.subtype: Approach: trying and falling and trying again [Action]
rows.description: A boy hops onto a cycle without training wheels and wobbles and falls. With each try he learns how to balance a little longer, and his knees heal quicker than his fear.

rows.subtype: Approach: watching a friend who rides well and copying [Action]
rows.description: A girl watches how her neighbour starts, pushes off and keeps her eyes ahead. She copies the steps one by one, and later asks the friend to correct her when she goes wrong.

rows.subtype: Approach: looking at the ground right in front of the wheel [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child stares at the front tyre and wobbles into a pole she is trying to avoid. Looking at the thing she fears seems to pull her toward it.

rows.subtype: Approach: looking far ahead where he wants to go [Revision]
rows.description: After crashing into a wall, the boy is told to look at the far end of the lane. He tries it, and his hands steer more smoothly toward the place his eyes are pointing.

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: mapping needs, resources and who can help [Thinking]
rows.description: A daughter lists her father's medical visits, daily support needs, siblings' availability and costs. The map shows that weekday mornings are the real gap.

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: family meeting to share responsibilities [Action]
rows.description: She calls her brother and aunt, states the tasks and time needed, and asks each to take a part: he handles finances and hospital visits, she handles daily calls and medicines organisation.

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: doing everything alone out of duty [Pitfall]
rows.description: Believing it is her responsibility, a daughter manages all care after work. Within months she is exhausted, makes errors at work and becomes short-tempered with her parents.

rows.subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing arrangements as health needs change [Revision]
rows.description: After the father's condition worsens, the family reviews and shifts from a daytime attendant to a professional care option, discussing it with the parents and their doctor.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: means-end analysis of housing, food and transport [Thinking]
rows.description: A fresher moving from Varanasi to Pune breaks the move into what is needed to survive the first month: a bed, meals and a commute, and compares options for each within Rs 25,000. Each gap becomes a concrete task.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: shared accommodation search through college and alumni networks [Action]
rows.description: The person messages alumni from the same college who live in the city and joins a hostel group, then visits two shared flats in person before paying a deposit. Local contacts reduce both cost and the risk of a bad deal.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: sign the first flat to end the stress [Pitfall]
rows.description: Worn out by searching, the newcomer pays a broker fee and a large deposit for a flat seen only on video. The place turns out to be far from work and the lease terms are strict, which shows the cost of choosing under fatigue.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: renegotiate rent and drop a costly service after tracking the first month [Revision]
rows.description: After one month of tracking, the person sees rent and a gym take too much, asks a flatmate to share a room and drops the membership. Adjusting early keeps the move sustainable.

rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from the audience's need [Thinking]
rows.description: The student asks what the panel needs to decide and builds the talk around that single message, instead of showing everything that was done.

rows.subtype: Approach: storyboarding slides on paper [Action]
rows.description: Before opening slides, the student sketches each slide on paper as a problem, method, result and next step, and cuts every slide that does not serve the story.

rows.subtype: Approach: putting all text on slides and reading it out [Pitfall]
rows.description: Scared of forgetting, the student fills slides with paragraphs and reads them, and the audience loses interest since they can read faster than the speaker talks.

rows.subtype: Approach: emotion-aware handling of nerves [Revision]
rows.description: Feeling a shaky voice after the first slide, the student slows down, pauses, takes a sip of water and continues, having planned that nerves would be normal.

rows.subtype: Approach: scheduling regular call times [Action]
rows.description: The couple agree on three calls a week around the student's lab hours and the partner's shift, and keep one weekend slot for a long conversation.

rows.subtype: Approach: values-first talk about expectations [Thinking]
rows.description: Before the move, the two discuss what each needs, such as daily check-ins, honesty about feelings and space for exams, and write down shared expectations for both.

rows.subtype: Approach: assuming silence means loss of interest [Pitfall]
rows.description: When the partner's replies slow during exams, the student imagines the worst and sends many anxious messages, which adds pressure and starts an argument.

rows.subtype: Approach: revising the routine when it feels forced [Revision]
rows.description: Realising that daily calls have become a chore, the couple switch to shorter daily messages and two proper calls a week, and the relationship feels lighter again.
